key_highlights: ASX set to open higher as tech stocks lead after Wall Street surge; oil snaps losing run (33, 16, 26)
Aussie flash PMI sags, signalling softening domestic activity (1)
No evidence of wage-price spiral in Australia, easing RBA inflation pressure (20)
RBA rate hikes continue to squeeze household spending, pressuring consumer sector (28)
Global diesel shortage from Iran/Ukraine wars to persist into 2027; Saudi oil shock lifts Australian fuel prices (51, 36)
Gold exploration activity intensifies: Platina, Dalaroo, Broken Hill, Advance all report progress (35, 37, 39, 38, 69, 70, 71)
China rebalancing towards robotics, raising structural demand concerns for iron ore and bulk commodities (45)
Jetstar industrial action escalates with staff waiving baggage/seat fees (30, 32)
Federal and state governments face debt cliff; Intergenerational Report locks in mass migration (44, 64)
El Niño 'Godzilla' event threatens agricultural output (43)

sectors.trend: Gold exploration names active (Platina, Dalaroo, Broken Hill, Advance) but China's pivot to robotics threatens long-term iron ore/coal demand. Diesel shortage supports energy metals.
sectors.implications: Gold miners benefit from safe-haven flows amid geopolitical risk; BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face structural demand headwinds from China rebalancing. Small-cap gold explorers see capital inflows.

sectors.trend: RBA rate hikes squeezing household spending; no wage-price spiral gives RBA room to pause. Debt cliff pressures government bond yields.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin pressure from weaker consumer credit growth. Rate pause expectations support valuations. Fiscal risk from debt cliff (44) could pressure sovereign credit.

sectors.trend: Oil sliding on global supply concerns but diesel shortage from Iran/Ukraine wars persists to 2027. Saudi oil shock lifts Australian pump prices. Energy prices dumping on US Democrat sweep expectations.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WLE.AX face mixed signals: crude weakness vs diesel scarcity. Woodside and Santos benefit from diesel premium. Renewable energy adoption by farmers (13) supports long-term transition.

sectors.trend: Pain management trade surging; Novo Nordisk's 2030 pitch receives muted reception.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX remains defensive anchor. Pain-trade growth supports smaller ASX-listed pharma/biotech. Novo's weak reception (52) may redirect capital to Australian healthcare names.

sectors.trend: RBA hikes squeeze spending; Jetstar industrial action escalates; Qantas announces Sydney-New York non-stop flights. Record sheep prices support rural income.
sectors.implications: QAN.AX benefits from route expansion but faces Jetstar (JPA.AX) industrial risk. WES.AX, WOW.AX pressured by weak consumer spending. Agricultural income (10) supports rural consumer demand.

sectors.trend: Tech stocks lead ASX higher post Wall Street surge. Data centres strain net-zero targets. AI infrastructure breakthroughs (Cipher Digital) and Nvidia pushback on AI doomsday talk.
sectors.implications: ASX tech names (WTC.AX, XRO.AX) benefit from global tech momentum. Data centre energy demand (41) supports power generators. Apple price hikes (61) signal hardware cost inflation.

key_themes: Commodity demand structural shift: China pivoting to robotics, threatening bulk commodity volumes
Energy transition tension: diesel scarcity vs renewable adoption by farmers
Fiscal sustainability: federal/state debt cliff and migration-driven population growth
Geopolitical energy risk: Iran/Ukraine diesel shortage extending to 2027
RBA policy pivot: no wage-price spiral supports rate pause, but spending squeeze persists
Gold exploration renaissance across WA, SA, and international jurisdictions

risk_assessment.risk_factor: China demand rebalancing away from bulk commodities
risk_assessment.mitigation: Diversify away from pure iron ore/coal exposure; favour gold and critical minerals (rare earths via Dalaroo)

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Prolonged diesel shortage and energy price volatility
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge fuel costs; favour integrated energy majors (WDS.AX) over pure-play refiners

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Fiscal debt cliff and migration-driven spending
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor government bond yields; favour quality financials with strong capital buffers
Underweight agribusiness; favour food staples with diversified supply chains

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Jetstar industrial action and transport sector disruption
risk_assessment.mitigation: Avoid JPA.AX near-term; QAN.AX as relative value play

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold exploration and production names
opportunities.rationale: Active exploration pipeline (Platina, Dalaroo, Broken Hill, Advance) plus safe-haven demand amid geopolitical risk and China uncertainty

opportunities.recommendation: Add ASX tech exposure on global momentum
opportunities.rationale: Tech leading ASX higher; AI infrastructure and data centre demand provide structural tailwinds

opportunities.recommendation: Favour integrated energy majors on diesel scarcity premium
opportunities.rationale: Diesel shortage to 2027 supports margins for integrated players despite crude weakness

defensive_moves.rationale: China's structural pivot to robotics threatens long-term bulk commodity demand

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge consumer discretionary via staples and healthcare
defensive_moves.rationale: RBA rate hikes squeezing household spending; no wage-price spiral but weak demand persists
Jetstar industrial action escalates with fee waivers; Qantas route expansion offers relative value

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to trade range-bound with tech outperforming. Oil volatility and PMI softness cap upside. RBA pause expectations provide a floor. Jetstar industrial action adds transport sector noise.
market_outlook.long_term: Structural headwinds from China rebalancing and fiscal debt cliff weigh on materials and financials. Gold, critical minerals, and healthcare offer relative resilience. Energy transition and AI infrastructure provide thematic growth.
